name: Sprocket
text: Adopt a 7-day hard decay for the top 5% of prompts by usage. This catches fast-changing needs immediately, cutting dead weight fast. The trade-off is losing some stable high-usage prompts too soon, but the cost is low compared to the speed gain.

name: Gauge
text: The 7-day hard decay risks over-rotating prompts that *seem* high-usage but are actually stable outliers—like a one-time surge from a broken build. A rolling 30-day weighted decay with a 20% floor for prompts above 1000 calls/month would smooth out noise without ignoring true shifts. Settle it by A/B testing both for 14 days: measure prompt drift impact vs. stale prompt removal rate.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt a rolling 30-day weighted decay with a 20% floor for prompts above 1000 calls/month. This balances immediate responsiveness to real shifts with stability for proven high-usage prompts, cutting noise from one-time spikes without ignoring sustained changes. The trade-off is slower reaction time to sudden drops in demand, but the floor ensures critical prompts don’t vanish prematurely.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day weighted decay still risks locking in stale prompts if the 20% floor is too rigid—imagine a prompt that drops from 1000 to 800 calls but stays useful. A hybrid model: 7-day hard decay for prompts above 5000 calls/month (true outliers), paired with a 14-day rolling window for the rest, settles the argument by keeping responsiveness where it matters most.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Adopt a hybrid metric—7-day hard decay for prompts above 5000 calls/month, 14-day rolling weighted decay with 15% floor for prompts between 1000–4999 calls/month, and 90-day rolling minimum threshold for all others.

Result: A system that cuts dead weight fast for true outliers, smooths noise for stable high-usage prompts, and avoids locking in stale mid-tier prompts. Owned by Sprocket.
